title: Raphaël Glucksmann Officially Declares 2027 Presidential Candidacy
detail: Place Publique leader and MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, 46, officially announced his candidacy for France's 2027 presidential election during a prime-time interview on TF1's evening news. Glucksmann said he was preparing 'for months' and cast himself as the candidate who could lead an 'ecological transition,' with polling putting him at 10–12% support. He confirmed he will enter a joint Socialist Party–Place Publique primary planned for October, joining an increasingly crowded left-wing field that already includes Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

media.caption: Raphaël Glucksmann announces his 2027 presidential candidacy on TF1

title: Bruno Le Maire Publishes Manifesto for 'Another France' Ahead of 2027 Race
detail: Former Economy Minister Bruno Le Maire published a roughly sixty-page manifesto titled a text for 'another France,' setting out three priorities — restoring state 'authority,' securing 'prosperity' through pension and tax changes including raising the retirement age to 65 and a VAT increase paired with lower payroll taxes, and defending European 'sovereignty' via a proposed federation of a handful of core EU states. Le Maire said he is not (yet) a declared candidate but described the document as a 'necessary vision to win collectively in 2027,' positioning it against both Jean-Luc Mélenchon's left and Marine Le Pen's far right.

media.caption: Bruno Le Maire presents his manifesto 'for another France'
